In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
self-reporting of symptoms of RTIs and UTIs can be used for screening purposes but the presence of symptoms alone is insufficient to diagnose RTIs and UTI in women.

self-reports of vaginal discharge, genital prolapse, or UTI can be used in the community for screening and for diagnosis of these conditions, but a positive report should be followed by a clinical and laboratory evaluation.
self-report of symptoms of genital prolapse, RTI and UTI can be used for the diagnosis of these conditions, but that the diagnosis should be confirmed by physical examination and/or laboratory tests.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the self-reports of women in Oman for RTI, genital prolapse and urinary tract infections are reliable and can be used to screen women for these gynaecologic problems.
women’s self-report of gynaecological conditions can be used in epidemiological research, but should not be used as the sole criterion for diagnosis in clinical practice.
self-reports of vaginal discharge, genital prolapse, or urinary symptoms are useful for community diagnosis of RTIs, genital prolapse and urinary infections respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reliability of self-report of gynaecological symptoms in Omani women can be enhanced through the use of specific questions that are medically significant.
the self-report of symptoms can be used in the diagnosis of RTIs and genital prolapse.
